sources.entry: winpython - Portable Python distribution for Windows.

summary.one_liner: WinPython tools is the wppm package manager and build toolchain for WinPython, a portable Python distribution for Windows, and is not the distribution itself.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes this repository as the wppm Python package and the build toolchain for WinPython, not the distribution itself. WPPM (WinPython Package Manager) is a companion tool to browse the bundled packages, install packages from the included wheelhouse, or register a WinPython install. The README says pip is the recommended way to add or remove packages otherwise. The repository also holds a historic build toolchain driven by a .bat script and a TOML file, and, as of 2026-01-01, GitHub Actions workflows (for example github_workflows_build-YYYY_NN.yml) that build a numbered WinPython release from a fork. Users can also get the equivalent package set from provided pylock.toml or requirements-with-hash.txt files.
use_cases: Build a portable Python distribution for Windows
Install packages from a bundled wheelhouse
Reproduce a WinPython release from pinned wheel hashes
Register a WinPython install with a package manager
how_to_run: python -m pip install --no-deps --require-hashes  (with a requirements-with-hash file, per README)
notable: Package manager (WPPM) for browsing and installing from a bundled wheelhouse
GitHub Actions workflows to build a WinPython release from a fork
Hash-pinned wheel sets via pylock.toml or requirements files
caveats: The README says this is the tools repository, not the WinPython distribution itself; the distribution is obtained from downloads linked elsewhere.
Building requires Python 3.11+ for the toolchain and a GitHub account to use the Actions workflow.
The README points to pip as the recommended route for adding or removing packages outside WPPM.
